public_rationale: The claim covers two companies. For OpenAI it holds. Company documents reported by the New York Times and confirmed by CNBC put its 2024 loss at about $5 billion. For CoreWeave it does not hold on the plain reading of 'lose'. Its IPO filing showed a 2024 net loss of about $863 million, under $1 billion, with $324 million in operating income. CoreWeave's capital spending did consume billions in cash, so a cash-burn reading would favour him. But 'lose billions' ordinarily means net losses. The 'no tangible evidence this will ever change' part is a judgement about the future and was not scored.
limitations: The OpenAI figure is a press-reported expectation from company documents, not an audited result.
The result depends on reading 'lose' as net loss rather than cash burn.
The forward-looking 'will ever change' clause was not scored.
